parts.visual:
Two best friends start a company and split the equity 50/50. Two years later, the CTO stops working hard, while the CEO is working 80-hour weeks. The CEO realizes they have to fire their best friend to save the company.

The Statistics:
1. Co-founder Conflict: This is one of the top three reasons early-stage startups fail. The psychological pressure of a startup destroys weak relationships.
2. The Vesting Cliff: This is why 4-year vesting with a 1-year cliff is mandatory. If the co-founder relationship explodes in month 6, the departing founder leaves with 0% of the company, saving the startup.
parts.audio: A co-founder relationship is a marriage with no romance and ten times the financial stress. If you do not have difficult, brutal conversations about equity, expectations, and roles on Day 1, the startup will eventually explode.

questions.question: Two founders split equity 50/50 with absolutely no vesting agreement. One founder quits on Day 2 to go travel the world. What happens to the startup?
options: It is completely dead. The departing founder owns half the company forever while doing no work. No VC will ever invest in a company where half the equity is 'dead weight'. The remaining founder must start a new company.
questions.correct_answer: It is completely dead. The departing founder owns half the company forever while doing no work. No VC will ever invest in a company where half the equity is 'dead weight'. The remaining founder must start a new company.
questions.explanation: Never, ever incorporate without a vesting schedule.

questions.question: Listen to the lawyer explain how to handle a co-founder who is failing at their job. What is the legal procedure?
questions.tts_text: You cannot just lock them out of the building. You must hold a formal Board of Directors meeting. If the board votes to terminate their employment, they are fired. But they will still retain any equity that has legally vested.
options: Due Process. Even if they are your friend, they are a corporate officer. The termination must be handled via formal board resolutions and legal severance agreements to prevent them from suing the company later.
questions.correct_answer: Due Process. Even if they are your friend, they are a corporate officer. The termination must be handled via formal board resolutions and legal severance agreements to prevent them from suing the company later.
questions.explanation: Friendship ends where fiduciary duty begins.

questions.question: Why is a 50/50 equity split between two founders often considered a massive mistake?
options: It creates corporate paralysis. If the two founders fundamentally disagree on a strategic decision (like selling the company), there is no tie-breaker. Someone must always have 51% to ensure the company can actually make a decision.
questions.correct_answer: It creates corporate paralysis. If the two founders fundamentally disagree on a strategic decision (like selling the company), there is no tie-breaker. Someone must always have 51% to ensure the company can actually make a decision.
questions.explanation: Equality is great for friendship, terrible for governance.

questions.question: If a co-founder leaves under bad circumstances but holds 20% of vested stock, what does the remaining CEO usually do?
options: Negotiate a Buyout. Having a furious ex-founder owning 20% of the voting power is toxic. The company or the VCs will usually offer cash to 'buy back' the shares at a discount just to get the ex-founder off the cap table.
questions.correct_answer: Negotiate a Buyout. Having a furious ex-founder owning 20% of the voting power is toxic. The company or the VCs will usually offer cash to 'buy back' the shares at a discount just to get the ex-founder off the cap table.
questions.explanation: Clean cap tables are required for future fundraising.

questions.explanation: Trust is good. Contracts are better.
